title: Hurricane names and deaths
subtitle: A famous finding, and the analysis that made it
question: Do hurricanes with more feminine names cause more deaths?

decision_rule.metric: additional deaths from a hurricane with a feminine rather than a masculine name

reference_label: Simonsohn, Simmons and Nelson (2020) specification curve, 1,728 specifications

reference.label: Specification curve median across 1,728 specifications (Table 2, p. 6)

story: A famous paper reported that hurricanes with feminine names kill more people. Re-run with the original choices, the effect is +4.1 additional deaths (95% CI -3.0 to 11.2), p = 0.257: no clear evidence. 3 one-decision changes get a significant effect, and the published specification curve finds the same pattern: 37 of 1,728 reasonable analyses are significant.

column_notes.year: Year the hurricane made landfall in the United States.
column_notes.name: Name given to the hurricane.
column_notes.masfem: Mean rating of the name on a masculine (1) to feminine (11) scale by nine coders.
column_notes.min: Minimum central pressure at landfall in millibars.
column_notes.gender_mf: 1 if the name is a female name, 0 if a male name.
column_notes.alldeaths: Total number of deaths attributed to the hurricane.
column_notes.ndam: Property damage in millions of dollars normalised to 2013 values.
column_notes.masfem_mturk: Mean rating of the name on the same 1 to 11 scale by 32 online raters.
column_notes.wind: Maximum sustained wind speed at landfall in miles per hour.
column_notes.ndam15: Property damage in millions of dollars normalised to 2015 values.
